goal: Extend the existing durable SQLite DAG engine in src/engine.py without regressing the event store or earlier engine behavior. Add claim_batch(now,lease_seconds=30): atomically claim exactly the deterministic ready wave and return an ordered tuple of (task_id, unique_token) pairs; an empty wave has no side effects. Add renew(task_id,token,now,extend_seconds): require a matching live lease strictly before expiry, positive extension, and set lease_until=max(previous lease_until,now)+extend_seconds. Add cancel(task_id,now): pending or running tasks become cancelled, running token is invalidated, capacity is released, and all transitive pending dependents become blocked; repeated cancel is idempotent, while cancelling a succeeded task raises ValueError. Add durable history(after_sequence=0) returning an immutable tuple of Transition records with sequence, task_id, action, at, attempt. Record each successful claim, renew, complete, fail, expiry, cancel, and dependent block exactly once in chronological transaction order, with actions named claim/renew/complete/fail/expire/cancel/block. Expiry and blocking may be triggered by ready(now), and repeated calls cannot duplicate events. Migrate an existing engine database that lacks a history table without losing state. Ensure concurrent independent connections cannot duplicate batch claims. Preserve all existing public APIs and behavior, and do not edit tests.
criteria: Existing event store and DAG behavior remain correct
Batch claiming and renewal are atomic and capacity safe under concurrency
Cancellation invalidates leases and blocks descendants deterministically
Durable transition history is complete, ordered, deduplicated and survives restart
